narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: A local cultural practitioner from the Ankole region.

narration: The Cow Dance of Ankole
This is Ekitaguriro. Traditional.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Title card: Ekitaguriro · Uganda · Traditional

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated in the Ankole region of southwestern Uganda, an area formed by the union of the Nkore kingdom with the chiefdoms of Sheema, Buhweju, and Igara.
It reflects the pastoralist and agriculturalist history of the Bahima and Bairu groups.
on_screen: Map: Uganda · Africa
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is performed at social gatherings to celebrate births, marriages, and abundant harvests, symbolizing the cultural significance of cattle.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Ekitaguriro dance.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b9/Ekitaguriro_dance.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Men imitate the walking gait of cows by stepping from one leg to another.
Women sway from side to side while spreading their hands across and above their heads to represent the long-horned cattle.
Watch for Cow Gait, Horn Representation.

images.description: Ekitaguriro aka Cow Dance is a traditional dance originating from Nkore or Ankole region which is located in South Western Uganda. It is a celebratory dance that is performed by both men and women as an expression of gratitude for their cattle and to showcase local prosperity such as birth, marriage and abundant harvest.
